item.title: Senators Warn Apple Not to Buy Memory Chips From Chinese Firms
item.description: A bipartisan group of US senators urged Apple Inc. to abandon any efforts to buy chips from blacklisted Chinese semiconductor suppliers CXMT Corp. and Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., warning that the iPhone maker risked becoming reliant on a US adversary for crucial components.

item.title: Bond Rout Sends Warning to Warsh That Tough Talk Is Not Enough
item.description: The message from the bond market was clear: For all of Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s tough talk about taming inflation, he’s in no rush to use the power of the central bank to do it.

item.title: Asian Stocks to Fall as Fed Keeps Rates on Hold: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to track Wall Street lower after renewed concerns over artificial intelligence spending and uncertainty over the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook sent longer-dated Treasury yields to their highest levels in almost two decades.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 30
item.description: Oil steadied after its biggest daily jump in more than two weeks, as President Donald Trump vowed fresh strikes in Iran and US stockpiles fell.

item.title: ChatGPT, Roblox to Fall Under Strictest EU Rules for Platforms
item.description: OpenAI’s ChatGPT and video game company Roblox Corp. will be subject to stricter scrutiny and monitoring requirements under the European Union’s content moderation rules after surpassing a threshold of 45 million monthly users in the bloc.

item.title: Goldman-Backed Biotech Attovia Seeks $212.5 Million in US IPO
item.description: Attovia Therapeutics Inc., an early-stage drug developer focused on immune-mediated diseases with high unmet need, is seeking to raise as much as $212.5 million in a US initial public offering.

item.title: Analog Devices Discloses Breach After ‘Unauthorized Access’
item.description: Analog Devices Inc. said it uncovered unauthorized access to its systems last month and that, after an investigation, it found that some files were “exfiltrated” from the affected systems.

item.title: NZ Markets Watchdog CEO on Leave as Workplace Culture Reviewed
item.description: New Zealand’s financial markets watchdog has appointed an interim chief executive after Samantha Barrass went on leave following revelations of “cultural concerns” in the workplace.

item.title: What Traders Are Telling the Federal Reserve: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg journalists answer your questions about how markets are navigating the Federal Reserve under Kevin Warsh in a Live Q&A on Thursday, July 30 at 1:15 p.m. EDT

item.title: Binance.US Wants to Join Prediction Markets Race With CFTC Stamp
item.description: Binance.US is planning to apply for a license with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission that would help it start its own prediction market, the company’s chief executive officer said at a conference on Wednesday.

item.title: Microsoft Reports Over $130 Billion in New Data Center Leases
item.description: Microsoft Corp. reported more than $130 billion in new data center leases in the past quarter, signaling an accelerating pace of spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.

item.title: Meta’s Free Cash Flow Dwindles to Lowest in Nearly Four Years
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc.’s free cash flow has fallen to the lowest level since the third quarter of 2022, a result of its transformation from a social media app maker into an AI company.

item.title: Goldman Pitches $5.4 Billion Debt for Microsoft-Tied Data Center
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is gauging investor appetite for a potential $5.4 billion debt offering to help fund a Blackstone-backed QTS data center tied to Microsoft Corp., as bubble concerns push up costs for artificial intelligence infrastructure financings.

item.title: Apollo’s Slok Says Fed’s New Silence Fuels ‘Yo-Yo’ Bond Market
item.description: Apollo Global Management’s Torsten Slok said the Federal Reserve’s abandonment of forward guidance is fueling historic bond market volatility, sending Treasury yields swinging “up and down like a yo-yo.”

item.title: Thoma Bravo Cedes to Lender Revolt on $5 Billion Proofpoint Loan
item.description: Thoma Bravo’s Proofpoint Inc. has reworked a $5 billion loan deal, offering major concessions to lenders increasingly anxious about AI-driven tech disruption.

item.title: Meta Gives Lackluster Quarterly Sales Forecast; Shares Drop
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. gave a disappointing revenue forecast for the current quarter, intensifying investor concerns about the social media giant’s unprecedented spending on artificial intelligence.

item.title: Microsoft’s Cloud Accelerates to Fastest Growth Since 2022
item.description: Microsoft Corp.’s cloud unit grew at the fastest pace in four years, suggesting that the company’s computing infrastructure and artificial intelligence services continue to make inroads with businesses.

item.title: Arm Outlook Leaves Investors Unmoved Despite Topping Estimates
item.description: Arm Holdings Plc delivered a sales forecast that failed to impress investors, who have grown increasingly wary about chip-industry prospects in recent days.

item.title: Qualcomm Gives Tepid Profit Forecast in Sign of Phone Woes
item.description: Qualcomm Inc., the largest maker of smartphone processors, gave a weak profit forecast for the current quarter, signaling that component shortages and rising costs are taking a toll on its main market.

item.title: Stonepeak CEO Warns Capital Markets Hold Risk for AI Buildout
item.description: Banks, private equity and capital markets show very little sign of slowing down on financing the massive artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out that is thriving in the US, according to Stonepeak Infrastructure Partners Chief Executive Officer Mike Dorrell.

item.title: Carney Rejects Idea of Using Oil as Weapon Against US Tariffs
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the notion that Canada should curb the supply of vital resources to the US to retaliate against tariffs, arguing that it’s more important for the country to keep its reputation as a dependable producer.

item.title: Private Credit Has an Affiliation Problem
item.description: A potential slowdown in the private credit-insurance pipeline.

item.title: JPMorgan’s Michele Says Dissenting Fed Trio Sends Crucial Signal
item.description: JPMorgan Asset Management’s Bob Michele said the trio of dissents from Federal Reserve policymakers stood out in the central bank’s hold-the-line decision on Wednesday, signaling that pressure for higher interest rates is likely to persist.

item.title: Creator of Test That OpenAI Models Tried to Cheat Sounds Alarm
item.description: A group of university researchers that developed benchmarks to test the cybersecurity capabilities of AI systems have unexpectedly landed themselves at the center of OpenAI’s accidental hack into the startup Hugging Face Inc.

item.title: Ex-French Fighter Pilot Charged in China Spying Case, AFP Says
item.description: A former French fighter pilot was charged and placed under judicial supervision for allegedly collecting and providing classified information to a foreign power, AFP reported, citing the Paris public prosecutor’s office.

item.title: Dollar Drops to Lowest in Nearly a Week as Fed Holds Steady
item.description: The dollar fell, touching the lowest in almost a week, after the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged, although several officials voted for an increase.

item.title: Bond Traders Pare September Hike Bets After Fed Holds Rates
item.description: US bond traders lowered their expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its next meeting after officials kept their benchmark steady on Wednesday.

item.title: AI Model Escape, Then Target Tools to Help Themselves Improve
item.description: Goal-driven behavior, not malicious intent, is a key problem, according to security experts.

item.title: Fed Holds Rates, Three Officials Dissent Favoring a Hike
item.description: Federal Reserve officials left interest rates unchanged, but a fractured vote signaled growing conviction among some policymakers that higher rates are needed to curb resurgent inflation.
